chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Al-Sindy, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the sun changes (at midday), remember Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; and if you are with a group of people who are pre-occupying you, then stand up and supplicate.'

key_terms.تَغَيُّرُ الشَّمْسِ: The changing of the sun (referring to the time of Dhuhr/midday prayer)
key_terms.فَقُمْ: So stand up (indicating a physical act of worship)
key_terms.يَشْغَلُونَكَ: Pre-occupying you (distracting or keeping you busy)

ai.seo_question: What should one do when the sun changes at midday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the specific practice of dhikr upon the changing of the sun, often interpreted by Shia scholars as marking the transition to Dhuhr or Asr, emphasizing mindfulness in daily routines. It underscores the priority of spiritual obligation over social engagement, instructing the believer to physically disengage ('stand') and supplicate even amidst distractions, reflecting the Imami emphasis on consistent, active remembrance of Allah.
